alate: Head yellowish brown, compound eyes dark brown, ocelli pale, labrum greyish white, antennal segment 3 dark brown while the remaining segments are pale; thorax yellowish brown, legs yellow, wings brown and transparent. Head nearly circular, length and width almost equal; compound eyes nearly round, prominent; ocelli slightly round, not touching the compound eyes. Antennae slender, 15 to 20 segments, segment 3 slightly longer than segments 2 and 4, the terminal five or six segments stouter, the apical segment smaller, oval. Pronotum generally slightly wider than the head, sometimes almost as wide, with a notch in the middle of the anterior margin, posterior margin slightly flat. Tibial spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi 4-segmented.
distribution: In China recorded from Nanjing, Jiangsu; Shanghai; and Ninghai, Zhejiang; abroad it occurs in California and Arizona in the United States, and in Mexico.
soldier: Head capsule elongate, the apex of the frons often raised above the rest, forming twin peaks; frontal surface either inclined or steep, its rugae sometimes coarse and deep, sometimes smooth, or merely punctate. Antennae short, mostly 10 to 12 segments. Mandibles short and stout, much shorter relative to the head length than in Neotermes, with several clearly discernible marginal teeth, the mandibular basal hump either distinct or flat. Labrum mostly square. Pronotum flat and broad, femora not thickened; tibial spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi 4-segmented.
